newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF denies report on Daiwa trust business.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF denies report on Daiwa trust business.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance on Wednesday denied a newspaper report that it plans to allow Daiwa Bank Ltd to expand its trust banking operations as part of the government's "Big Bang" financial reforms.

The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday that the ministry was set to permit Daiwa Bank to offer loan trusts and trusts on movable property, such as railroad carriages and plant machinery.
"We have not been considering such a measure," said an official at MOF's Banking Bureau. "However, it may be included in the government's deregulation agenda in the future."
A spokesman for Daiwa Bank also said on Wednesday that the bank had not asked the ministry to allow the move.
Daiwa Bank is the only one among Japan's top 10 commercial banks allowed to have trust banking operations.

But the ministry has limited Daiwa's trust operations to pension trusts and property accumulation trusts in order to protect specialised trust banks, which have far smaller branch networks than the big commercial banks.
Last year, other commercial banks were allowed to enter the trust banking sector, albeit only through setting up subsidiaries.

In November, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto unveiled a five-year Big Bang plan to liberalise Japan's financial markets and try to catch up with reforms carried out more than a decade ago in Europe and North America.
